metrics.description: A map of user-defined score name to {@link MlScoringMetric}s to be used for monitoring model performance.

input.description:
A {@link MlModel.Monitor.Data} instance responsible for gathering a list
of model predictions, corresponding labels, and optional scoring context.

filter.description:
Filter to select the inputs in scope for this monitoring group.
It is input to {@link MlModel.Monitor.DataSpec#filter} for customization of {@link MlModel.Monitor.Data#dataGroupsFromSpec}.
If unspecified or null, no filtering is applied.

title:
Defines how to calculate performance of {@link MlModel}s, by specifying a map of {@link MlScoringMetric}s
and information required to fetch inputs for {@link MlScoringMetric} calculation. All the {@link MlScoringMetric}s defined in
this {@link MlModel.Monitor.Group} share the same inputs.
Used in {@link MlModel.Monitor.Job#groups}.

See {@link link MlModel.Monitor.Job}

Usage:
```python
# Define monitor groups for a multi-output `c3.MlModel` with two predictions - `sales` and `revenue`.
# Assumption - predictions are available for all 7 continents in the world.

# Example 1 - Using pre-defined sub-types of `c3.MlScoringMetric` for monitoring `sales` prediction.

# Define metrics
metric_map = { "precision" : c3.MlPrecisionMetric(), "recall": c3.MlRecallMetric()}

# Define how to fetch inputs for scoring metrics defined in `metric_map`
# Users need to define type `DataForSales` by mixing `MlModel.Monitor.Data`
# to fetch predictions/labels/contexts.

fetch_input = c3.MonitorExample.DataForSales()

# Define a monitoring group
# This monitoring group defines two metrics - `precision` and `recall` for `sales` prediction
# `modelOutputNames` is `sales` as this metric group sets up performance monitoring for `sales`
# `filter` indicates to select predictions from `North America`.
# `groupBy` indicates to calculate one metric per country per model, on predictions from `North America`.
monitor_group_sales = c3.MlModel.Monitor.Group(metrics=metric_map,
                                               input=fetch_input,
                                               filter="continent=North America",
                                               groupBy=["country"])

# Example 2 - Define a monitor group using custom scoring metric that uses both `sales` and `revenue` predictions.
# Define metrics
def custom_score(targetOutput=None, modelOutput=None, context=None):
   # Multi-input is a Named Tuple - names of `targetOutput` and `modelOutput` for multi-input score
   # is specified in `c3.MlScoringMetricSpec`.
   target_output_sales = targetOutput.t1.to_pandas()
   model_output_sales = modelOutput.m1.to_pandas()
   target_output_revenue = targetOutput.t2.to_pandas()
   model_output_revenue = modelOutput.m2.to_pandas()
   assert len(target_output_sales) == len(model_output_sales), "sales has different lengths"
   assert len(target_output_revenue) == len(model_output_revenue), "revenue has different lengths"
   assert len(target_output_sales) == len(target_output_revenue), "sales and revenue have different lengths"

   diff_of_pred1 = target_output_sales - model_output_sales.sum()
   diff_of_pred2 = target_output_revenue - model_output_revenue.sum()
   return (diff_of_pred1 + diff_of_pred2)/len(target_output_sales)

custom_metric = c3.MlCustomMetric.fromPyFunc(py_func=custom_score,
                                             spec=c3.MlScoringMetricSpec(targetOutputNames=["t1", t2"],
                                                                          modelOutputNames=["m1", m2"]))

# This monitoring group defines one combined custom metric for the `sales` and `revenue`.
# `targetOutputMapping` and `modelOutputMapping` are required fields for a multi-input
# scoring metric to indicate mapping between label/prediction name and respective target/model output
# name in `custom_metric`.

custom_monitor_metric = c3.MlMappedMetric(
  scoringMetric=custom_metric,
  targetOutputMapping={'t1': 'sales', 't2': 'revenue'},
  modelOutputMapping={'m1': 'sales', 'm2': 'revenue'}
)

metric_map = {"custom_score" : custom_monitor_metric}

# Define how to fetch predictions and labels
fetch_input = c3.MonitorExample.DataForAll()

# Define a monitoring group
# All predictions will be used as there is no `filter`.
# One score per model wil be calculated as there is no `groupBy`.
monitor_group_combined = c3.MlModel.Monitor.Group(metrics=metric_map,
                                                  input=fetch_input
                                                   )
```
NOTE: It is important to understand why `custom_metric` was not included in `monitor_group_sales`.
The reason is - All the metrics defined in a monitoring group share the same inputs.
Since inputs for `custom_score` (`sales` and `predictions`) are different ,
from `precision` and `recall` (`sales` only), they are in different monitor groups.
The difference is due to specification of `filter` and `groupBy`.
name: MlModel.Monitor.Group
